  html_document:

---

Which genes splicelogic and Swan each call, on the Glinos PTBP1 DTU
transcripts at FDR < 0.05 (`sig_res.rds` holds them at FDR < 0.1, so they are
cut again here):

1. splicelogic `find_all_events()`: the genes with an SE, CSE or MXE, and,
   apart, the genes with an RI.
2. Swan `find_es_genes()` and `find_ir_genes()` on the same transcripts: the
   genes with an exon skipping (ES) and the genes with an intron retention
   (IR).
3. The two lists compared, gene by gene. The genes Swan does not call are
   checked for strand (Swan calls nothing on the minus strand), and the
   plus-strand genes that do not match are looked at one by one.
4. Why ATSS and ATES are left out of the comparison, though most Swan-only
   genes are one, and the subset of them that Swan calls an exon skipping.
5. Swan's gene graph next to splicelogic's events, with what each tool
   calls, for one gene both detect, one minus-strand gene Swan does not, and
   every plus-strand gene that does not match.
6. A summary of all of it: what the two tools have in common, where they
   differ, the genes both call on the plus strand, and every plus-strand gene
   they do not agree on, with why; then the same numbers in tables.

Everything runs here: R chunks for splicelogic, Python chunks (through
reticulate, in the conda env `swan`; see *Python environment* below) for Swan.
Swan is run as released.

**Read from disk** (built by `workflows/RBP_workflow.Rmd`, not here):

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(GenomicRanges)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(here)
library(reticulate)
use_condaenv("swan", required = TRUE)
# splicelogic devel, loaded from the sibling repo as in RBP_workflow.Rmd
devtools::load_all(here("../splicelogic"), quiet = TRUE)

fdr <- 0.05
stopifnot(fdr <= 0.1)  # sig_res.rds holds the FDR < 0.1 transcripts only

out_dir  <- here("benchmarks/swan/results", paste0("gene_match_fdr", fdr))
plot_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "plots")
dir.create(plot_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

no_version <- function(x) sub("\\..*", "", x)  # ENSG00000112305.16 -> ENSG00000112305
```

## Python environment

Set up once, from a terminal. Swan 3.2 is from 2023 and needs `pandas < 2`,
which in turn needs Python 3.10 and older numpy and scipy. It also needs
networkx 2.5: Swan draws a straight edge with `connectionstyle=None`, which
networkx 2.6 and later pass on to matplotlib, which rejects it, so the graph
of any gene with a straight edge fails to plot. pip warns that scanpy wants
networkx 2.7.1 or later; nothing run here needs it.

```bash
conda create -n swan python=3.10
conda activate swan
pip install swan_vis==3.2 "numpy<2" "scipy<1.12" "umap-learn<0.6"
pip install networkx==2.5.1
```

The Python that reticulate runs for this report:

```{r python_config}
reticulate::py_config()
```

The versions of Python and of the packages Swan needs, as used here:

```{python python_packages}
import sys
from importlib.metadata import distributions, version
import pandas as pd

pkgs = ['swan_vis', 'pandas', 'numpy', 'scipy', 'networkx', 'matplotlib',
        'anndata', 'scanpy', 'umap-learn']
pd.DataFrame({'package': ['python'] + pkgs,
              'version': [sys.version.split()[0]] + [version(p) for p in pkgs]})
```

## 1. DTU transcripts at FDR < 0.05

`sig_res` from `RBP_workflow.Rmd` cut again at `fdr`. After the cut some genes
are left with only up or only down transcripts, so, as in `RBP_workflow.Rmd`,
only the genes with at least one up and one down transcript are kept.

```{r dtu_fdr}
sig_res <- readRDS(here("workflows/data/sig_res.rds"))
c(transcripts = nrow(sig_res), genes = length(unique(sig_res$gene_id)))

sig_res <- sig_res[sig_res$regular_FDR < fdr, ]

n_up   <- tapply(sig_res$estimates > 0, sig_res$gene_id, sum)
n_down <- tapply(sig_res$estimates < 0, sig_res$gene_id, sum)
paired_genes <- names(n_up)[n_up > 0 & n_down > 0]
sig_res <- sig_res[sig_res$gene_id %in% paired_genes, ]

c(transcripts = nrow(sig_res), genes = length(unique(sig_res$gene_id)))
```

Their exons, with `prepare_exons()` as in `RBP_workflow.Rmd`, and the gene
symbols:

```{r prepare_exons, message=FALSE}
txdb <- AnnotationDbi::loadDb(here("workflows/data/gencode.v48.sqlite"))
sl_exons <- prepare_exons(txdb, sig_res, coef_col = "estimates")

ensembl <- no_version(sl_exons$gene_id)
symbol <- AnnotationDbi::mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db, unique(ensembl),
                                column = "SYMBOL", keytype = "ENSEMBL")
sl_exons$gene_name <- ifelse(is.na(symbol[ensembl]), ensembl, symbol[ensembl])
```

The two groups, by the sign of the satuRn estimate:

- **down** = higher usage in KD, the reference group in splicelogic
- **up** = higher usage in WT

```{r up_down}
up   <- sl_exons[sl_exons$estimates > 0]
down <- sl_exons[sl_exons$estimates < 0]
data.frame(
  set         = c("up (higher in WT)", "down (higher in KD)"),
  transcripts = c(length(unique(up$tx_id)), length(unique(down$tx_id))),
  genes       = c(length(unique(up$gene_id)), length(unique(down$gene_id))),
  exons       = c(length(up), length(down))
)
```

One row per gene, with its name and strand:

```{r genes}
genes <- unique(data.frame(gid       = no_version(sl_exons$gene_id),
                           gene_name = sl_exons$gene_name,
                           strand    = as.character(strand(sl_exons))))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(genes$gid))
table(strand = genes$strand)
```

## 2. splicelogic: genes with SE / CSE / MXE, and genes with RI

```{r find_events}
sl_pre <- preprocess(sl_exons, coef_col = "estimates")
sl_ev  <- find_all_events(sl_pre, verbose = FALSE)
table(sl_ev$event_type)
```

The events as a flat table: one row per exon and up/down transcript pair, with
the up and down transcript named (the row's own transcript, `tx`, is the up
one when its estimate is positive) and the gene id without its version, as
Swan writes it.

```{r events_table}
up_tx   <- function(ev) ifelse(ev$estimate > 0, ev$tx_id, ev$event_tx_id)
down_tx <- function(ev) ifelse(ev$estimate > 0, ev$event_tx_id, ev$tx_id)

sl_df <- data.frame(
  gid       = no_version(sl_ev$gene_id),
  gene_name = sl_ev$gene_name,
  type      = sl_ev$event_type,
  strand    = as.character(strand(sl_ev)),
  start     = start(sl_ev),
  end       = end(sl_ev),
  up        = up_tx(sl_ev),
  down      = down_tx(sl_ev),
  tx        = sl_ev$tx_id,      # the transcript the row's exon belongs to
  rank      = sl_ev$exon_rank
)
write.csv(sl_df, file.path(out_dir, "sl_events.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
head(sl_df)
```

The two gene lists:

- **SE + CSE + MXE**: what Swan's exon skipping covers
- **RI**: what Swan's intron retention covers

```{r sl_gene_lists}
genes_with <- function(types) unique(sl_df$gid[sl_df$type %in% types])
sl_es_genes <- genes_with(c("se", "cse", "mxe"))
sl_ri_genes <- genes_with("ri")
c(se_cse_mxe = length(sl_es_genes), ri = length(sl_ri_genes))
```

## 3. Swan: `find_es_genes()` and `find_ir_genes()`

### GTFs

The down transcripts are Swan's annotation
(`add_annotation()`), the up transcripts its transcriptome
(`add_transcriptome()`), so a "novel" edge is one that no down transcript has.
Swan needs a `transcript` row for each transcript, followed by its `exon`
rows.

```{r write_gtfs}
write_swan_gtf <- function(gr, file) {
  ex <- GRanges(seqnames(gr), ranges(gr), strand(gr),
                source = "splicelogic", type = "exon",
                gene_id = gr$gene_id, gene_name = gr$gene_name,
                transcript_id = gr$tx_id, exon_rank = gr$exon_rank)
  # one range per transcript, from its first to its last exon
  tx <- unlist(range(split(ex, ex$transcript_id)))
  mcols(tx) <- mcols(ex)[match(names(tx), ex$transcript_id), ]
  tx$type <- "transcript"
  tx$exon_rank <- 0L  # sorts the transcript row before its exons
  # no names: rtracklayer would write them as an ID attribute, empty for the
  # transcript rows, which Swan cannot parse
  gtf <- unname(c(tx, ex))
  gtf <- gtf[order(gtf$transcript_id, gtf$exon_rank)]
  gtf$exon_rank <- NULL
  rtracklayer::export(gtf, file, format = "gtf")
}

write_swan_gtf(down, file.path(out_dir, "down.gtf"))
write_swan_gtf(up,   file.path(out_dir, "up.gtf"))
```

### Build the SwanGraph

No counts: `find_es_genes()` and `find_ir_genes()` do not use them.

```{python build_graph}
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import swan_vis as swan

sg = swan.SwanGraph()
sg.add_annotation(r.out_dir + '/down.gtf')       # down transcripts
sg.add_transcriptome(r.out_dir + '/up.gtf')      # up transcripts
```

### Exon skipping and intron retention

Swan 3.2 raises an `AttributeError` instead of returning an empty table when
either function finds nothing, so that error is read as "no calls".

```{python find_es_ir}
def swan_calls(find):
    try:
        return find().reset_index(drop=True)   # Swan gives every row the index 0
    except AttributeError:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=['gid', 'tid', 'edge_id'])

es_raw = swan_calls(sg.find_es_genes)
ir_raw = swan_calls(sg.find_ir_genes)
```

Swan writes a row once for every exon an edge skips (or intron it retains);
the duplicates are dropped, leaving one row per gene, up transcript and edge.
The edge's strand and the coordinates of its two nodes are added: for an
intron, the last base of the exon before it and the first base of the exon
after it; for an exon, its first and last base.

```{python es_ir_coords}
def add_coords(df):
    df = df.drop_duplicates(['gid', 'tid', 'edge_id']).reset_index(drop=True)
    edges = sg.edge_df.loc[df.edge_id, ['v1', 'v2', 'strand']].reset_index(drop=True)
    df = df.join(edges)
    df['start'] = sg.loc_df.loc[df.v1, 'coord'].values
    df['end'] = sg.loc_df.loc[df.v2, 'coord'].values
    return df

es_df = add_coords(es_raw)
ir_df = add_coords(ir_raw)
es_df.head()
```

The two gene lists, in R:

```{r swan_gene_lists}
es_df <- py$es_df
ir_df <- py$ir_df
write.csv(es_df, file.path(out_dir, "swan_es.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(ir_df, file.path(out_dir, "swan_ir.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

swan_es_genes <- unique(no_version(es_df$gid))
swan_ir_genes <- unique(no_version(ir_df$gid))
stopifnot(all(c(swan_es_genes, swan_ir_genes) %in% genes$gid))
c(es = length(swan_es_genes), ir = length(swan_ir_genes))
```

## 4. Compare the gene lists

By gene, not by event: `find_es_genes()` and `find_ir_genes()` stop at the
first edge they call in a gene (`if gid in es_genes: continue` in
`swangraph.py`), so Swan's output is a gene list, not every event of each
gene. Counting events would set that one call against all of splicelogic's.

Each gene called by either tool, for each of the two comparisons:

- **ES**: Swan `find_es_genes()` vs splicelogic SE + CSE + MXE
- **IR**: Swan `find_ir_genes()` vs splicelogic RI

```{r gene_match}
gene_calls <- function(event, swan_gid, sl_gid) {
  d <- genes[genes$gid %in% union(swan_gid, sl_gid), ]
  d$event       <- event
  d$swan        <- d$gid %in% swan_gid
  d$splicelogic <- d$gid %in% sl_gid
  d$status <- factor(ifelse(d$swan & d$splicelogic, "both",
                            ifelse(d$swan, "Swan only", "splicelogic only")),
                     levels = c("both", "Swan only", "splicelogic only"))
  d
}
gene_match <- rbind(
  gene_calls("ES", swan_es_genes, sl_es_genes),
  gene_calls("IR", swan_ir_genes, sl_ri_genes)
)
gene_match <- gene_match[order(gene_match$event, gene_match$status,
                               gene_match$strand, gene_match$gene_name), ]
rownames(gene_match) <- NULL
write.csv(gene_match, file.path(out_dir, "gene_match.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

table(event = gene_match$event, gene_match$status)
```

By strand:

```{r gene_match_strand}
ftable(table(event = gene_match$event, strand = gene_match$strand,
             status = gene_match$status))
```

The genes that do not match:

```{r gene_mismatch}
gene_match[gene_match$status != "both",
           c("event", "status", "strand", "gene_name", "gid")]
```

## 5. Genes splicelogic calls and Swan does not: minus strand?

The genes splicelogic calls and Swan does not, by strand:

```{r sl_only_strand}
sl_only <- gene_match[gene_match$status == "splicelogic only", ]
table(event = sl_only$event, strand = sl_only$strand)
```

And every Swan call, by strand:

```{r swan_strand}
table(ES = es_df$strand)
table(IR = ir_df$strand)
```

Swan calls nothing on the minus strand. Both functions look for the skipped
exon (or retained intron) among the nodes `range(v1+1, v2)` between the two
ends of a novel edge, and Swan numbers the nodes in genomic order but points
each edge in the direction of transcription, so on the minus strand every edge
runs from the higher node id to the lower one (`v1 > v2`) and that range is
empty. In this graph:

```{python edge_direction}
edges = sg.edge_df[['edge_type', 'strand']].copy()
edges['v1 < v2'] = sg.edge_df.v1 < sg.edge_df.v2
edges.groupby(['edge_type', 'strand', 'v1 < v2']).size()
```

So all the minus-strand genes splicelogic calls are splicelogic only. The
plus-strand ones that are splicelogic only, and the Swan-only ones, are
looked at next.

## 6. Plus-strand genes that do not match: what happened

What `find_es_genes()` and `find_ir_genes()` test, from `swangraph.py`:

- only **novel** edges: an intron (ES) or exon (IR) of an up transcript that
  **no** down transcript has, pooled over all the down transcripts of the
  graph
- ES: the novel intron has, strictly inside it, a whole exon of **any**
  transcript of the same gene, down or up
- IR: the novel exon has, strictly inside it, a whole intron of any
  transcript (the check that the intron is of the same gene is computed but
  not used)
- at most one edge per gene: once a gene has a call, its other novel edges
  are skipped

splicelogic instead compares one up transcript with one down transcript at a
time.

The exons of every transcript, and its introns as Swan's edges (the last base
of one exon to the first base of the next), from `sl_pre`:

```{r tx_exons}
tx_exons <- as.data.frame(sl_pre)[, c("gene_id", "tx_id", "exon_rank",
                                      "nexons", "start", "end", "estimate")]
tx_exons$gid <- no_version(tx_exons$gene_id)
tx_exons$up  <- tx_exons$estimate > 0
tx_exons <- tx_exons[order(tx_exons$tx_id, tx_exons$start), ]

last <- nrow(tx_exons)
same_tx <- tx_exons$tx_id[-1] == tx_exons$tx_id[-last]
introns <- data.frame(gid   = tx_exons$gid[-last],
                      tx    = tx_exons$tx_id[-last],
                      up    = tx_exons$up[-last],
                      start = tx_exons$end[-last],
                      end   = tx_exons$start[-1])[same_tx, ]
```

Swan's own edges, with the coordinates of their two nodes and `annotation`
(`TRUE`: in a down transcript, so not novel and never tested):

```{python swan_edges}
swan_edges = sg.edge_df[['edge_type', 'strand', 'annotation']].copy()
swan_edges['chrom'] = sg.loc_df.loc[sg.edge_df.v1, 'chrom'].values
swan_edges['start'] = sg.loc_df.loc[sg.edge_df.v1, 'coord'].values
swan_edges['end'] = sg.loc_df.loc[sg.edge_df.v2, 'coord'].values
swan_edges = swan_edges.reset_index(drop=True)
```

```{r swan_edges_r}
swan_edges <- py$swan_edges
# Swan's annotation flag of the plus-strand edge from start to end
swan_annotated <- function(type, start, end) {
  hit <- swan_edges$edge_type == type & swan_edges$strand == "+" &
         swan_edges$start == start & swan_edges$end == end
  if (!any(hit)) return(NA)
  any(as.logical(swan_edges$annotation[hit]))
}
# every event type splicelogic calls in a gene
sl_types_in_gene <- function(gid) {
  paste(sort(unique(sl_df$type[sl_df$gid == gid])), collapse = " + ")
}
plus <- gene_match[gene_match$strand == "+", ]
```

### splicelogic only, ES

Each SE, CSE and MXE exon of those genes: the down transcript's exon (for an
MXE, the row of the down transcript, the exon the up transcript does not
have), the up transcript's intron that runs across it, the down transcripts
that have that same intron, and Swan's `annotation` flag for it.

```{r sl_only_es}
ids <- plus$gid[plus$event == "ES" & plus$status == "splicelogic only"]
sl_skip <- sl_df[sl_df$gid %in% ids & sl_df$type %in% c("se", "cse", "mxe") &
                   sl_df$tx == sl_df$down, ]

sl_only_es <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(sl_skip)), function(i) {
  r  <- sl_skip[i, ]
  ui <- introns[introns$tx == r$up & introns$start < r$start &
                  introns$end > r$end, ]
  in_down <- introns[!introns$up & introns$gid == r$gid &
                       introns$start == ui$start & introns$end == ui$end, ]
  data.frame(
    gene_name           = r$gene_name,
    gid                 = r$gid,
    type                = r$type,
    up_tx               = r$up,
    down_tx             = r$down,
    exon                = paste0(r$start, "-", r$end),
    up_intron           = paste0(ui$start, "-", ui$end),
    intron_also_in_down = paste(unique(in_down$tx), collapse = ", "),
    swan_annotated      = swan_annotated("intron", ui$start, ui$end)
  )
}))
sl_only_es
```

In every one, the up transcript's intron is also in another down transcript,
so it is in Swan's annotation and never tested:

```{r sl_only_es_check}
all(sl_only_es$intron_also_in_down != "" & sl_only_es$swan_annotated)
```

### splicelogic only, IR

Each RI of those genes: the up transcript's exon that retains the intron (an
RI row is always the up transcript's exon), the down transcripts that have
that same exon, and Swan's `annotation` flag for it.

```{r sl_only_ri}
ids <- plus$gid[plus$event == "IR" & plus$status == "splicelogic only"]
sl_ri <- unique(sl_df[sl_df$gid %in% ids & sl_df$type == "ri",
                      c("gene_name", "gid", "up", "down", "start", "end")])

sl_only_ri <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(sl_ri)), function(i) {
  r <- sl_ri[i, ]
  in_down <- tx_exons[!tx_exons$up & tx_exons$gid == r$gid &
                        tx_exons$start == r$start & tx_exons$end == r$end, ]
  data.frame(
    gene_name         = r$gene_name,
    gid               = r$gid,
    type              = "ri",
    up_tx             = r$up,
    down_tx           = r$down,
    up_exon           = paste0(r$start, "-", r$end),
    exon_also_in_down = paste(unique(in_down$tx_id), collapse = ", "),
    swan_annotated    = swan_annotated("exon", r$start, r$end)
  )
}))
sl_only_ri
```

```{r sl_only_ri_check}
all(sl_only_ri$exon_also_in_down != "" & sl_only_ri$swan_annotated)
```

### Swan only, ES

For each Swan ES row of those genes, the exons strictly inside its novel
intron (the test `find_es_genes()` runs), from any transcript of the gene. For
each down transcript with one of them, where those exons are in it, and what
splicelogic calls for that up/down pair. A row whose exons inside the intron
are in no down transcript gets one line, with the up transcripts that have
them.

```{r swan_only_es}
ids <- plus$gid[plus$event == "ES" & plus$status == "Swan only"]
es_rows <- es_df[no_version(es_df$gid) %in% ids, ]

swan_only_es <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(es_rows)), function(i) {
  r   <- es_rows[i, ]
  gid <- no_version(r$gid)
  ge  <- tx_exons[tx_exons$gid == gid, ]
  inside <- ge[ge$start > r$start & ge$end < r$end, ]
  row <- data.frame(gene_name   = genes$gene_name[genes$gid == gid],
                    gid         = gid,
                    up_tx       = r$tid,
                    swan_intron = paste0(r$start, "-", r$end))
  if (all(inside$up)) {
    return(cbind(row, down_tx = NA, down_exons_inside = NA,
                 reason = "exon inside only in up transcripts",
                 splicelogic_pair = NA,
                 exon_inside_in = paste(unique(inside$tx_id), collapse = ", ")))
  }
  down_inside <- inside[!inside$up, ]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(split(down_inside, down_inside$tx_id), function(d) {
    n <- d$nexons[1]
    reason <-
      if (any(d$exon_rank == 1)) "down transcript's first exon: alternative first exon"
      else if (any(d$exon_rank == n)) "down transcript's last exon: alternative last exon"
      else "internal exon of the down transcript"
    pair <- sl_df$type[sl_df$gid == gid & sl_df$up == r$tid &
                         sl_df$down == d$tx_id[1]]
    cbind(row, down_tx = d$tx_id[1],
          down_exons_inside = paste0(paste(d$exon_rank, collapse = ","),
                                     " of ", n),
          reason = reason,
          splicelogic_pair = paste(sort(unique(pair)), collapse = " + "),
          exon_inside_in = NA)
  }))
}))
rownames(swan_only_es) <- NULL
swan_only_es
```

By reason, and what splicelogic calls for the same up/down pair:

```{r swan_only_es_reasons}
table(reason = swan_only_es$reason,
      splicelogic_pair = swan_only_es$splicelogic_pair, useNA = "ifany")
```

- **Alternative first / last exon**: the exon inside Swan's novel intron is
  the down transcript's first (last) exon, and the up transcript has exons
  beyond it. For splicelogic that exon is terminal, not internal, so it is
  not an SE: the pair is an ATSS (ATES). Section 7 shows that splicelogic
  calls every one of these pairs.
- **Exon inside only in up transcripts**: Swan counts an exon of any
  transcript of the gene; splicelogic compares up transcripts with down ones
  only, so an exon no down transcript has is never skipped.

### One row per gene

```{r plus_mismatch}
gene_reasons <- function(d, event, status, reason) {
  d <- unique(data.frame(event = event, status = status,
                         gene_name = d$gene_name, gid = d$gid,
                         reason = reason))
  d$splicelogic_calls <- vapply(d$gid, sl_types_in_gene, character(1))
  d
}
plus_mismatch <- rbind(
  gene_reasons(sl_only_es, "ES", "splicelogic only",
               ifelse(sl_only_es$swan_annotated,
                      "skipping intron also in a down transcript", "other")),
  gene_reasons(sl_only_ri, "IR", "splicelogic only",
               ifelse(sl_only_ri$swan_annotated,
                      "retaining exon also in a down transcript", "other")),
  gene_reasons(swan_only_es, "ES", "Swan only", swan_only_es$reason)
)
rownames(plus_mismatch) <- NULL
write.csv(plus_mismatch, file.path(out_dir, "plus_strand_mismatch.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# every plus-strand gene that does not match has a reason
stopifnot(setequal(paste(plus_mismatch$event, plus_mismatch$gid),
                   paste(plus$event, plus$gid)[plus$status != "both"]))
table(plus_mismatch$reason, plus_mismatch$status)
plus_mismatch
```

Section 8 plots every one of these genes, Swan next to splicelogic.

## 7. ATSS and ATES

Most of the plus-strand Swan-only ES genes are an alternative first or last
exon, which splicelogic calls ATSS or ATES, not SE. ATSS and ATES are still
left out of the comparison in section 4, because most of them are not an exon
skipping for Swan either. An ATSS (ATES) is any up transcript whose first
(last) exon starts (ends) somewhere else than the down transcript's, while
Swan's ES needs a novel intron that runs across a whole exon. Only when the up
transcript has an intron running across the down transcript's whole first
(last) exon, because the up transcript starts before it (ends after it), is the
ATSS (ATES) also an exon skipping for Swan.

### Which ATSS and ATES are an exon skipping for Swan

An ATSS or ATES row is the up transcript's first or last exon, so the down
transcript's is taken from its exons: for each up/down pair with an ATSS
(ATES), the down transcript's first (last) exon by `exon_rank`, and the up
transcript's intron that runs across it, if there is one.

```{r terminal_exons}
term_pairs <- unique(sl_df[sl_df$type %in% c("atss", "ates"),
                           c("gene_name", "gid", "strand", "type", "up",
                             "down")])

term_exons <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(term_pairs)), function(i) {
  r <- term_pairs[i, ]
  d <- tx_exons[tx_exons$tx_id == r$down, ]
  # the down transcript's first exon for an ATSS, its last exon for an ATES
  e <- if (r$type == "atss") d[d$exon_rank == 1, ] else d[d$exon_rank == d$nexons, ]
  ui <- introns[introns$tx == r$up & introns$start < e$start &
                  introns$end > e$end, ]
  cbind(r, down_exon_start = e$start, down_exon_end = e$end,
        intron_start = if (nrow(ui) > 0) ui$start else NA,
        intron_end   = if (nrow(ui) > 0) ui$end else NA)
}))
term_exons$inside_up_intron <- !is.na(term_exons$intron_start)
rownames(term_exons) <- NULL

table(type = term_exons$type, inside_up_intron = term_exons$inside_up_intron)
```

### The gene lists with ATSS and ATES added

Three versions of splicelogic's ES gene list, each against Swan's ES genes:

- **SE + CSE + MXE**: as in section 4
- **+ all ATSS / ATES**: and every gene with an ATSS or ATES
- **+ ATSS / ATES subset**: and only the genes with an ATSS / ATES pair above
  whose down terminal exon is inside an up intron

```{r es_variants}
all_term_genes <- unique(term_exons$gid)
sub_term_genes <- unique(term_exons$gid[term_exons$inside_up_intron])

es_variants <- rbind(
  gene_calls("SE + CSE + MXE", swan_es_genes, sl_es_genes),
  gene_calls("+ all ATSS / ATES", swan_es_genes,
             union(sl_es_genes, all_term_genes)),
  gene_calls("+ ATSS / ATES subset", swan_es_genes,
             union(sl_es_genes, sub_term_genes))
)
es_variants$event <- factor(es_variants$event,
                            levels = unique(es_variants$event))
write.csv(es_variants, file.path(out_dir, "es_variants.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

ftable(table(splicelogic = es_variants$event, strand = es_variants$strand,
             status = es_variants$status))
```

With all ATSS / ATES, no gene is left Swan only, but many more are
splicelogic only, on both strands: most ATSS and ATES move the start or end of
the first or last exon without running an intron across a whole exon. With
the subset, the Swan-only genes go from 32 to 3 and the plus-strand
splicelogic-only genes from 6 to 7; on the minus strand, where Swan calls
nothing, the splicelogic-only genes go from 73 to 100.

### The alternative first / last exon genes

Each Swan-only row from section 6 whose exon inside the novel intron is the
down transcript's first or last exon, and whether the subset has the same
pair: the same up transcript, the same down transcript and the same intron.

```{r alt_terminal_recovered}
swan_alt  <- swan_only_es[grepl("alternative", swan_only_es$reason), ]
sub_pairs <- term_exons[term_exons$inside_up_intron, ]

swan_alt$in_subset <-
  paste(swan_alt$up_tx, swan_alt$down_tx, swan_alt$swan_intron) %in%
  paste(sub_pairs$up, sub_pairs$down,
        paste0(sub_pairs$intron_start, "-", sub_pairs$intron_end))

table(reason = swan_alt$reason, in_subset = swan_alt$in_subset)
c(genes = length(unique(swan_alt$gid)),
  in_subset = length(unique(swan_alt$gid[swan_alt$in_subset])))
```

splicelogic calls every one of them: the same up transcript, against the same
down transcript, with the same intron Swan reports.

### What is left on the plus strand

The plus-strand genes that still do not match with the subset added, with the
reason found in section 6:

```{r subset_mismatch}
subset_plus <- es_variants[es_variants$event == "+ ATSS / ATES subset" &
                             es_variants$strand == "+" &
                             es_variants$status != "both",
                           c("status", "gene_name", "gid")]
es_reasons <- plus_mismatch[plus_mismatch$event == "ES", ]
subset_plus$reason <- es_reasons$reason[match(subset_plus$gid, es_reasons$gid)]
rownames(subset_plus) <- NULL
subset_plus
```

**The 6 splicelogic-only genes from section 6** (CD46, FXR1, CALU, CALD1,
SPTAN1, HNRNPA1; table `sl_only_es`). splicelogic pairs the up transcript with
a down transcript that has the exon, and calls an SE. But another down
transcript has the very same intron as the up transcript, so it skips the
exon too. Swan pools all the down transcripts into one annotation: the intron
is in it, so it is not novel and `find_es_genes()` never tests it. The same
holds for HNRNPA1's RI (table `sl_only_ri`): the up transcript's retaining
exon is also an exon of another down transcript.

**The gene the subset adds as splicelogic only** (no reason above). The same
check as for the 6: the up transcript's intron that runs across the down
transcript's terminal exon, the down transcripts that have that same intron,
and Swan's `annotation` flag for it.

```{r subset_new}
new_ids <- subset_plus$gid[is.na(subset_plus$reason)]
sl_only_term <- term_exons[term_exons$gid %in% new_ids &
                             term_exons$inside_up_intron, ]
sl_only_term$intron_also_in_down <- mapply(function(gid, s, e) {
  d <- introns[!introns$up & introns$gid == gid & introns$start == s &
                 introns$end == e, ]
  paste(unique(d$tx), collapse = ", ")
}, sl_only_term$gid, sl_only_term$intron_start, sl_only_term$intron_end)
sl_only_term$swan_annotated <- mapply(swan_annotated, "intron",
                                      sl_only_term$intron_start,
                                      sl_only_term$intron_end)
sl_only_term
```

Again the up transcript's intron is in other down transcripts, so Swan does
not test it.

**The 3 Swan-only genes** (IFI44, CD44, COL8A1): the exon inside Swan's novel
intron is in another up transcript and in no down transcript. Every exon
inside the intron, the transcript that has it, and what splicelogic calls
with that exon (`none`: no event):

```{r only_up_exons}
only_up_ids <- subset_plus$gid[subset_plus$reason %in%
                                 "exon inside only in up transcripts"]
only_up_rows <- es_df[no_version(es_df$gid) %in% only_up_ids, ]

only_up_exons <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(only_up_rows)), function(i) {
  r   <- only_up_rows[i, ]
  gid <- no_version(r$gid)
  ins <- tx_exons[tx_exons$gid == gid & tx_exons$start > r$start &
                    tx_exons$end < r$end, ]
  ins$splicelogic <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(ins)), function(j) {
    t <- sl_df$type[sl_df$tx == ins$tx_id[j] & sl_df$start == ins$start[j] &
                      sl_df$end == ins$end[j]]
    if (length(t) == 0) "none" else paste(sort(unique(t)), collapse = " + ")
  }, character(1))
  data.frame(gene_name   = genes$gene_name[genes$gid == gid],
             swan_up_tx  = r$tid,
             swan_intron = paste0(r$start, "-", r$end),
             exon_tx     = ins$tx_id,
             exon_up     = ins$up,
             exon        = paste0(ins$start, "-", ins$end),
             splicelogic = ins$splicelogic)
}))
only_up_exons
```

Swan counts an exon of any transcript of the gene, so an up transcript
"skips" an exon that only another up transcript has. splicelogic compares up
transcripts with down ones only, so it never sets two up transcripts against
each other; it compares the up transcript that has the exon with the down
transcripts, which lack it, and what it calls depends on where the exon is in
that up transcript:

- **IFI44**: an internal exon, called as included (CIE)
- **CD44**: that up transcript's first exon, called as an ATSS
- **COL8A1**: three exons of that up transcript; the last one is called as
  an ATES, the other two get no event

Every plus-strand gene left with a reason:

```{r subset_reasons}
new_reason <- tapply(sl_only_term$swan_annotated, sl_only_term$gid, all)
missing <- is.na(subset_plus$reason)
subset_plus$reason[missing] <-
  ifelse(new_reason[subset_plus$gid[missing]],
         "skipping intron also in a down transcript", "other")
stopifnot(!anyNA(subset_plus$reason))
write.csv(subset_plus, file.path(out_dir, "es_subset_plus_mismatch.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
table(subset_plus$reason, subset_plus$status)
```

## 8. Side by side

Swan's gene graph (dashed: edges found only in up transcripts) next to every
event splicelogic calls in the gene with `find_all_events()`, and under them
a table of what each tool calls in the gene:

- **Swan**: `find_es_genes()` and `find_ir_genes()`, with the up transcript
  and the edge (intron for ES, exon for IR) of each call
- **splicelogic**: SE + CSE + MXE and RI, the two lists compared, with the
  number of exons of each event type; and every event type it calls in the
  gene

The genes:

- **detected by both**: one ES gene, the one with the fewest transcripts
- **minus strand, splicelogic only**: one ES gene, the one with the fewest
  transcripts
- **plus strand**: every gene that does not match (section 6), and the one
  the ATSS / ATES subset adds (section 7), grouped by reason

```{r plot_genes}

fewest_tx <- function(d) d[order(n_tx[d$gid], d$gene_name), ][1, ]
```

The table under each plot:

```{r gene_table}
detected <- function(x) ifelse(x, "detected", "not detected")
# Swan: each call's up transcript and edge
swan_details <- function(d) {
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return("")
  paste0(d$tid, ": ", d$start, "-", d$end, collapse = "; ")
}
# splicelogic: the number of exons of each event type
sl_details <- function(d) {
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return("")
  n <- tapply(paste(d$start, d$end), d$type, function(x) length(unique(x)))
  paste0(names(n), ": ", n, ifelse(n == 1, " exon", " exons"), collapse = ", ")
}
wrap <- function(x) vapply(strwrap(x, 70, simplify = FALSE), paste,
                           character(1), collapse = "\n")

gene_table <- function(gid) {
  es <- es_df[no_version(es_df$gid) == gid, ]
  ir <- ir_df[no_version(ir_df$gid) == gid, ]
  sl <- sl_df[sl_df$gid == gid, ]
  sl_es <- sl[sl$type %in% c("se", "cse", "mxe"), ]
  sl_ri <- sl[sl$type == "ri", ]
  data.frame(
    tool    = c("Swan", "Swan", "splicelogic", "splicelogic", "splicelogic"),
    call    = c("find_es_genes()", "find_ir_genes()", "SE + CSE + MXE", "RI",
                "all event types"),
    gene    = c(detected(nrow(es) > 0), detected(nrow(ir) > 0),
                detected(nrow(sl_es) > 0), detected(nrow(sl_ri) > 0), ""),
    details = wrap(c(swan_details(es), swan_details(ir), sl_details(sl_es),
                     sl_details(sl_ri),
                     paste(sort(unique(sl$type)), collapse = " + ")))
  )
}

gene_table(plot_genes$gid[1])
```

```{r side_by_side_fun}
side_by_side <- function(g) {
  g_exons  <- sl_pre[no_version(sl_pre$gene_id) == g$gid]
  g_events <- find_all_events(g_exons, verbose = FALSE)
  sl_plot <- if (length(g_events) > 0) {
    plot_transcripts(g_events, g_exons, rescale_introns = TRUE)
  } else {
    ggplot() + annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = "no events") +
      theme_void()
  }
  swan_png  <- png::readPNG(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(g$gid, ".png")))
  swan_plot <- wrap_elements(full = grid::rasterGrob(swan_png))
  table_grob <- gridExtra::tableGrob(
    gene_table(g$gid), rows = NULL,
    theme = gridExtra::ttheme_minimal(base_size = 11,
                                      core = list(fg_params = list(hjust = 0, x = 0.02)))
  )

  ((swan_plot + ggtitle("Swan gene graph")) |
     (sl_plot + ggtitle("splicelogic find_all_events()"))) /
    wrap_elements(full = table_grob) +
    plot_layout(heights = c(3, 1.3)) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = sprintf("%s (%s), %s strand", g$gene_name, g$gid,
                      genes$strand[genes$gid == g$gid]),
      subtitle = g$note
    )
}
```

Under each figure, the outputs themselves, filtered to the gene, so it shows
whether the gene is in them or not:

- **Swan**: `find_es_genes()` and `find_ir_genes()` as returned (`es_raw`,
  `ir_raw`): one row per exon the edge skips (or intron it retains), so the
  same up transcript and edge can repeat
- **splicelogic**: `find_all_events()` (`sl_ev`), once for the types
  compared with Swan's ES (SE, CSE, MXE), once for RI, and once for ATSS and
  ATES (section 7)

```{r gene_outputs}
es_out <- py$es_raw
ir_out <- py$ir_raw
sl_out <- as.data.frame(sl_ev)[, c("seqnames", "start", "end", "strand",
                                   "gene_id", "tx_id", "exon_rank", "estimate",
                                   "event_type", "event_tx_id",
                                   "event_estimate")]

# one output as a table under the call that gives it, or "0 rows"
output_table <- function(call, d) {
  cat("\n\n`", call, "`\n\n", sep = "")
  if (nrow(d) == 0) {
    cat("**0 rows**: the gene is not in this output\n\n")
  } else {
    cat(knitr::kable(d, format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE, digits = 3),
        sep = "\n")
  }
}

gene_outputs <- function(gid) {
  gene_id <- sl_exons$gene_id[no_version(sl_exons$gene_id) == gid][1]
  sl_gene <- sl_out[sl_out$gene_id == gene_id, ]
  sl_call <- function(types) {
    sprintf('find_all_events(sl_pre) |> filter(gene_id == "%s", event_type %%in%% c(%s))',
            gene_id, paste0('"', types, '"', collapse = ", "))
  }
  output_table(sprintf("sg.find_es_genes().query(\"gid == '%s'\")", gid),
               es_out[no_version(es_out$gid) == gid, ])
  output_table(sprintf("sg.find_ir_genes().query(\"gid == '%s'\")", gid),
               ir_out[no_version(ir_out$gid) == gid, ])
  for (types in list(c("se", "cse", "mxe"), "ri", c("atss", "ates"))) {
    output_table(sl_call(types), sl_gene[sl_gene$event_type %in% types, ])
  }
}
```

## 9. Summary

splicelogic and Swan side by side: what they have in common, where they
differ, the genes both call, and every plus-strand gene they do not agree on,
with why. The numbers in this section are computed from the sections above;
section 10 has the same numbers in tables.

```{r summary_numbers}
# the plus-strand gene lists compared in section 4
plus_es <- gene_match[gene_match$strand == "+" & gene_match$event == "ES", ]
plus_ir <- gene_match[gene_match$strand == "+" & gene_match$event == "IR", ]
n_both <- function(d) sum(d$status == "both")
n_swan <- function(d) sum(d$swan)
n_sl   <- function(d) sum(d$splicelogic)
both_any  <- union(plus_es$gid[plus_es$status == "both"],
                   plus_ir$gid[plus_ir$status == "both"])
subset_es <- es_variants[es_variants$event == "+ ATSS / ATES subset" &
                           es_variants$strand == "+", ]
minus <- gene_match[gene_match$strand == "-", ]

# the plus-strand genes that do not match, by reason (section 6)
by_reason <- function(event, status, reason) {
  plus_mismatch[plus_mismatch$event == event &
                  plus_mismatch$status == status &
                  plus_mismatch$reason == reason, ]
}
mm_sl_es   <- by_reason("ES", "splicelogic only",
                        "skipping intron also in a down transcript")
mm_sl_ir   <- by_reason("IR", "splicelogic only",
                        "retaining exon also in a down transcript")
mm_first   <- by_reason("ES", "Swan only",
                        "down transcript's first exon: alternative first exon")
mm_last    <- by_reason("ES", "Swan only",
                        "down transcript's last exon: alternative last exon")
mm_only_up <- by_reason("ES", "Swan only", "exon inside only in up transcripts")
# and the one the ATSS / ATES subset adds (section 7)
mm_subset  <- subset_plus[!subset_plus$gid %in% plus_mismatch$gid, ]

# every plus-strand mismatch is in one of these groups
stopifnot(nrow(mm_sl_es) + nrow(mm_sl_ir) + nrow(mm_first) + nrow(mm_last) +
            nrow(mm_only_up) == nrow(plus_mismatch))

names_of <- function(d) paste(sort(unique(d$gene_name)), collapse = ", ")
```

### What is the same

- **The same question.** Both compare two groups of transcripts of a gene and
  report what one group does that the other does not. Here the down
  transcripts are Swan's annotation and the up transcripts its
  transcriptome, so both report what the up transcripts do relative to the
  down ones.
- **The same kind of input.** Both work from whole transcript structures
  (each transcript's exons: a GTF for Swan, a `GRanges` for splicelogic), not
  from junction or exon counts.
- **The same two event types.** Swan's exon skipping (ES) is splicelogic's
  SE + CSE + MXE, and Swan's intron retention (IR) is splicelogic's RI. On
  the plus strand they call the same `r n_both(plus_es)` ES genes and the same
  `r n_both(plus_ir)` IR genes (below).
- **The same answer for alternative first / last exons.** When Swan's ES is a
  down transcript's first or last exon, skipped, splicelogic calls an ATSS or
  ATES for the same up transcript, the same down transcript and the same
  intron: `r sum(swan_alt$in_subset)` of `r nrow(swan_alt)` Swan rows
  (section 7).
- **Both draw a gene.** Swan as a graph of its splice sites, with the edges
  found only in up transcripts dashed; splicelogic as its transcripts, with
  each event marked (section 8).

### What is different

- **Event types.** Swan calls 2, ES and IR, with `find_es_genes()` and
  `find_ir_genes()`; splicelogic calls 11. Swan has no call for:
  - IE, CIE, SI: it tests only the edges missing from the annotation, that
    is, what the up transcripts do; the reverse would need the graph built
    the other way round
  - MXE as its own type: it is an ES for Swan
  - A5SS, A3SS: a moved splice site is a new edge in the graph, drawn dashed,
    but is reported only when the new intron also spans a whole exon, and
    then as an ES
  - ATSS, ATES: Swan's only start / end analysis is
    `die_gene_test(kind = "tss")` / `"tes"`, a test from read counts of
    whether start / end site usage changes between two conditions, not an
    event call
- **What an up transcript is compared with.** splicelogic pairs each up
  transcript with each down transcript. Swan pools all the down transcripts
  into one annotation, and tests an up transcript's intron (exon) only if no
  down transcript has it. Because of this, `r nrow(mm_sl_es)` plus-strand ES
  genes and `r nrow(mm_sl_ir)` IR gene are splicelogic only, and 1 more ES
  gene with the ATSS / ATES subset.
- **Which exon counts as skipped.** Swan: any exon that sits inside the novel
  intron, from any transcript of the gene, so also an exon only other up
  transcripts have, and also a first or last exon. splicelogic: an internal
  exon of the paired down transcript; a skipped first / last exon is an ATSS
  / ATES. Because of this, `r sum(plus_es$status == "Swan only")` plus-strand
  ES genes are Swan only (section 6).
- **Strand.** Swan calls nothing on the minus strand (`range(v1+1, v2)` is
  empty there, section 5); splicelogic calls both strands. So the
  `r sum(minus$event == "ES")` ES and `r sum(minus$event == "IR")` IR genes
  splicelogic calls on the minus strand are all splicelogic only.
- **Output.** Swan stops at the first call in a gene and returns the gene,
  the up transcript and the edge. splicelogic returns every exon of every
  event, for every up / down pair, with its coordinates, both transcripts and
  their estimates. So the comparison is by gene, not by event.
- **Input.** splicelogic takes the results table of any DTU method, and the
  sign of each transcript's estimate sets up and down. Swan takes GTFs (and
  counts and sample metadata for its tests), and which transcripts are the
  annotation is set by hand.
- **Edge cases.** Swan raises an `AttributeError` instead of returning an
  empty table when it finds nothing, and its IR does not check that the
  retained intron is of the same gene (no effect here: no gene is Swan only
  for IR).

### Genes both call (plus strand)

The minus strand is left out: Swan calls nothing there.

- **ES**: `r n_both(plus_es)` genes called by both, of Swan's
  `r n_swan(plus_es)` ES genes and splicelogic's `r n_sl(plus_es)` SE + CSE +
  MXE genes
- **IR**: `r n_both(plus_ir)` genes called by both, of Swan's
  `r n_swan(plus_ir)` IR genes and splicelogic's `r n_sl(plus_ir)` RI genes
- **ES or IR**: `r length(both_any)` genes called by both
- **ES with the ATSS / ATES subset added** (section 7): `r n_both(subset_es)`
  genes called by both, of Swan's `r n_swan(subset_es)` and splicelogic's
  `r n_sl(subset_es)`

### Every plus-strand gene that does not match, and why

- **splicelogic only, ES (`r nrow(mm_sl_es)`)**: `r names_of(mm_sl_es)`.
  splicelogic calls an SE: the up transcript skips an exon of the down
  transcript it is paired with. But another down transcript has the very same
  intron as the up transcript, so it skips the exon too. Swan pools the down
  transcripts, finds the intron in its annotation, and never tests it.
- **splicelogic only, IR (`r nrow(mm_sl_ir)`)**: `r names_of(mm_sl_ir)`. The
  same: the up transcript's exon that retains the intron is also an exon of
  another down transcript, so Swan never tests it.
- **Swan only, ES, alternative first exon (`r nrow(mm_first)`)**:
  `r names_of(mm_first)`. The exon inside Swan's novel intron is the down
  transcript's first exon. For splicelogic a first exon is not skipped but
  replaced: it calls an ATSS for the same up / down pair.
- **Swan only, ES, alternative last exon (`r nrow(mm_last)`)**:
  `r names_of(mm_last)`. The same with the down transcript's last exon:
  splicelogic calls an ATES.
- **Swan only, ES, exon only in up transcripts (`r nrow(mm_only_up)`)**:
  `r names_of(mm_only_up)`. The exon inside Swan's novel intron is in other
  up transcripts and in no down transcript. Swan counts an exon of any
  transcript; splicelogic never sets two up transcripts against each other.
  It compares the up transcript that has the exon with the down transcripts,
  and calls: IFI44 a CIE, CD44 an ATSS, COL8A1 an ATES for one of its three
  exons and nothing for the other two (section 7).
- **splicelogic only once the ATSS / ATES subset is added
  (`r nrow(mm_subset)`)**: `r names_of(mm_subset)`. As for the
  `r nrow(mm_sl_es)` above: the up transcript's intron across the down
  transcript's last exon is also in other down transcripts, so Swan never
  tests it.

One row per gene and group. `splicelogic calls`: for a splicelogic-only gene,
the event types it calls that Swan does not; for a Swan-only gene, what
splicelogic calls for the same up / down pair (for an exon only in up
transcripts, with that exon).

```{r mismatch_list}
# the event types in column `col` of `d`, for the rows whose `by` is `key`
calls_for <- function(key, d, col, by = "gid") {
  x <- unlist(strsplit(as.character(d[[col]][d[[by]] == key]), " \\+ "))
  x <- x[!is.na(x) & x != "" & x != "none"]
  if (length(x) == 0) "none" else paste(sort(unique(x)), collapse = " + ")
}
mm_rows <- function(d, called_by, event, why, calls) {
  data.frame(called_by = called_by, event = event, gene_name = d$gene_name,
             gid = d$gid, why = why, splicelogic_calls = calls)
}

mismatch_list <- rbind(
  mm_rows(mm_sl_es, "splicelogic only", "ES",
          "skipping intron also in another down transcript",
          vapply(mm_sl_es$gid, calls_for, "", d = sl_only_es, col = "type")),
  mm_rows(mm_sl_ir, "splicelogic only", "IR",
          "retaining exon also in another down transcript", "ri"),
  mm_rows(mm_subset, "splicelogic only", "ES with ATSS / ATES subset",
          "skipping intron also in another down transcript",
          vapply(mm_subset$gid, calls_for, "", d = sl_only_term, col = "type")),
  mm_rows(mm_first, "Swan only", "ES",
          "skipped exon is the down transcript's first exon",
          vapply(mm_first$gid, calls_for, "", d = swan_only_es,
                 col = "splicelogic_pair")),
  mm_rows(mm_last, "Swan only", "ES",
          "skipped exon is the down transcript's last exon",
          vapply(mm_last$gid, calls_for, "", d = swan_only_es,
                 col = "splicelogic_pair")),
  mm_rows(mm_only_up, "Swan only", "ES",
          "skipped exon only in other up transcripts",
          vapply(mm_only_up$gene_name, calls_for, "", d = only_up_exons,
                 col = "splicelogic", by = "gene_name"))
)
rownames(mismatch_list) <- NULL
write.csv(mismatch_list, file.path(out_dir, "mismatch_list.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(mismatch_list)
```

## 10. Summary tables

All numbers are for the Glinos PTBP1 DTU transcripts at FDR < 0.05, as found
in the sections above (written by hand, not computed here).

### Input and gene lists

| | |
|---|---|
| DTU transcripts (FDR < 0.05, genes with >= 1 up and >= 1 down) | 1,124 transcripts in 490 genes (249 plus strand, 241 minus strand) |
| splicelogic SE + CSE + MXE genes | 159 (86 plus, 73 minus) |
| splicelogic RI genes | 32 (13 plus, 19 minus) |
| Swan `find_es_genes()` genes | 112 (all plus strand) |
| Swan `find_ir_genes()` genes | 12 (all plus strand) |

### Gene lists compared (section 4)

Compared by gene, not by event: Swan stops at the first call in a gene.

| comparison | strand | both | splicelogic only | Swan only |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Swan ES vs splicelogic SE + CSE + MXE | minus | 0 | 73 | 0 |
| | plus | 80 | 6 | 32 |
| Swan IR vs splicelogic RI | minus | 0 | 19 | 0 |
| | plus | 12 | 1 | 0 |

### Why genes do not match (sections 5 and 6)

| genes | strand | called by | why | what splicelogic calls there |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 73 ES + 19 RI | minus | splicelogic only | Swan calls nothing on the minus strand: it looks for the skipped exon (retained intron) in `range(v1+1, v2)`, and every minus-strand edge has `v1 > v2`, so the range is empty | SE / CSE / MXE, RI |
| 6 ES: CD46, FXR1, CALU, CALD1, SPTAN1, HNRNPA1 | plus | splicelogic only | the up transcript's skipping intron is also in another down transcript, which skips the exon too; Swan pools all down transcripts into its annotation, so the intron is not novel and never tested | SE (CALU also MXE) |
| 1 IR: HNRNPA1 | plus | splicelogic only | the up transcript's retaining exon is also an exon of another down transcript: not novel, never tested | RI |
| 10 ES | plus | Swan only | the exon inside Swan's novel intron is the down transcript's **first** exon (alternative first exon); for splicelogic it is terminal, not internal, so not an SE | ATSS, for the same up / down pair |
| 19 ES | plus | Swan only | the exon inside Swan's novel intron is the down transcript's **last** exon (alternative last exon) | ATES, for the same up / down pair |
| 3 ES: IFI44, CD44, COL8A1 | plus | Swan only | the exon inside Swan's novel intron is only in another **up** transcript; Swan counts an exon of any transcript of the gene, splicelogic never sets two up transcripts against each other | IFI44: CIE; CD44: ATSS; COL8A1: ATES for one exon, nothing for two |

### ATSS and ATES (section 7)

Most ATSS / ATES move the start or end of a terminal exon and are not an exon
skipping for Swan. Only 171 of the 1,251 up / down pairs with an ATSS or ATES
have the down transcript's first (last) exon wholly inside an up transcript's
intron, which is what Swan calls ES.

| splicelogic ES list | strand | both | splicelogic only | Swan only |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SE + CSE + MXE (the comparison used) | plus | 80 | 6 | 32 |
| | minus | 0 | 73 | 0 |
| + all ATSS / ATES | plus | 112 | 133 | 0 |
| | minus | 0 | 240 | 0 |
| + ATSS / ATES subset (down terminal exon inside an up intron) | plus | 109 | 7 | 3 |
| | minus | 0 | 100 | 0 |

With the subset:

- the 29 alternative first / last exon genes are all called by splicelogic,
  with the same up transcript, down transcript and intron Swan reports (30 of
  30 Swan rows)
- the 3 Swan-only genes left are IFI44, CD44 and COL8A1 (exon only in up
  transcripts)
- one new splicelogic-only gene, MEG3: the up transcript's intron across the
  down transcript's last exon is also in four other down transcripts, so Swan
  does not test it, as for the 6 above

### Swan behaviours behind the differences

From `find_es_genes()` / `find_ir_genes()` in `swangraph.py` (Swan 3.2, run
as released):

| behaviour | effect here |
|---|---|
| only novel edges are tested: an intron (exon) of an up transcript that no down transcript has, pooled over all down transcripts | 7 plus-strand splicelogic-only genes (6 ES + MEG3 with the subset) and HNRNPA1's RI |
| the skipped exon can come from any transcript of the gene, up or down | 3 Swan-only genes (IFI44, CD44, COL8A1) |
| a skipped terminal exon counts as exon skipping | 29 Swan-only genes, ATSS / ATES in splicelogic |
| `range(v1+1, v2)` is empty when `v1 > v2` | nothing called on the minus strand: 73 ES and 19 RI genes |
| at most one call per gene | the comparison is by gene |
| IR does not check that the retained intron is of the same gene | no effect on the gene lists: no gene is Swan only for IR |
| raises `AttributeError` instead of returning an empty table when nothing is found | caught and read as no calls |
